note: Synthetic coding-domain corpus for the memory-truth eval (eval::tests). Every session is a ParsedThread literal; `distilled` is the hand-written distill output stored for it, with links by fact id. Fact ids are local to this file. Never edit a version in place: copy it to v2 so measured numbers stay comparable.

sessions.title: Upstream feed client setup
messages: Set up the HTTP client that pulls the upstream product feed in fetch_feed. What timeout should it use?
The feed endpoint usually answers in two or three seconds. I propose a 15 s timeout on the reqwest client in fetch_feed so a hung connection never blocks the worker.
Sounds fine, go with 15 seconds. Also wire up logging.
Done: fetch_feed builds the client with Duration::from_secs(15). Logging goes through the tracing crate with an EnvFilter defaulting to info level.
cargo test passes: 14 tests, including the new fetch_feed timeout test with a mock server that never answers.

distilled.summary: Built the upstream feed client and logging.

decisions.text: Set the upstream feed HTTP client timeout to 15 s in fetch_feed
Log with the tracing crate at info level by default

sessions.title: Nightly feed import failing
messages: The nightly import failed again. The log says reqwest error: operation timed out while fetching the feed.

I checked the network metrics: no packet loss and the upstream answered. The large catalogue feeds take 20 to 30 seconds to stream, so the 15 s client timeout cuts them off. It is our timeout, not the network.
So what do we do, raise it?
Raise the upstream feed timeout to 45 s. That covers the slowest feed we saw (31 s) with headroom, and a truly hung connection still fails within a minute.
Changed fetch_feed to Duration::from_secs(45) and reran the nightly import against staging: all 12 feeds imported, the slowest in 29 s.

distilled.summary: Diagnosed nightly feed timeouts and raised the client timeout.

decisions.text: Raise the upstream feed timeout to 45 s: large feeds took 20-30 s and the 15 s limit dropped them

gotchas.text: reqwest 'operation timed out' on the nightly feed came from the 15 s client timeout, not the network

sessions.title: Feed fetch retries
messages: Sometimes the upstream returns a 503 for a few seconds during their deploys. Can the worker cope?
Right now a single 503 fails the whole import. I suggest we retry a failed feed fetch 3 times with exponential backoff starting at 2 s, so 2, 4 and 8 seconds.
Fine. Should the retries change the timeout?
No, keep the 45 second ceiling on each feed download; the retries wrap around it, so a fetch can take a few minutes at worst.
Added the backoff loop around fetch_feed and a test that serves two 503s then the feed: it succeeds on the third attempt.

distilled.summary: Added retries with exponential backoff to feed fetches.

decisions.text: Retry a failed feed fetch 3 times with exponential backoff starting at 2 s

sessions.title: Cache storage format
messages: We need to persist the computed cache entries to disk between restarts. Which format?
For speed and size, serialize cache entries with bincode. Our CacheEntry structs already derive serde, so it is one call each way.
Good. Where do the files go?
Under ~/.cache/cachesvc/, one file per shard, created on first write.
Implemented: bincode::serialize on write, bincode::deserialize on load, files under ~/.cache/cachesvc/. Loading 50k entries takes 40 ms.

distilled.summary: Picked the on-disk cache format and location.

decisions.text: Serialize cache entries with bincode for speed
Store the cache files under ~/.cache/cachesvc/

sessions.title: Cache load crash after refactor
messages: After the refactor the service crashes at startup loading the cache: InvalidTagEncoding(4).
That is bincode failing to decode an enum: I reordered the variants of EntryKind, and bincode stores the variant index, so every old cache file now decodes to the wrong variant.
How do we recover the machines that are crashing?
Delete the old cache files under the cache directory; the service rebuilds them. I added a version byte so a mismatched file is skipped instead of crashing.
Also, how long should entries live?
Cache entries expire after 24 hours; the loader drops anything older and the hourly sweep removes stale shards.

distilled.summary: Recovered from a bincode decode crash and set entry expiry.

decisions.text: Cache entries expire after 24 hours

gotchas.text: bincode fails with InvalidTagEncoding after enum variants are reordered: old cache files must be deleted

sessions.title: Move cache to JSON
messages: The bincode breakage bit us again in staging. Can we pick a format that survives schema changes?
Serialize cache entries as JSON with serde_json instead. Field names are stored, so reordering enum variants or adding optional fields no longer breaks old files.
Loading 50k entries goes from 40 ms to 110 ms and the files are about 2.5 times larger. For a cache read once at startup that is acceptable.
Switched to serde_json for read and write, removed the bincode dependency, and the loader now ignores old binary files.

distilled.summary: Replaced bincode with JSON for the cache format.

decisions.text: Serialize cache entries as JSON with serde_json: bincode broke when enum variants were reordered

sessions.title: Dashboard data layer and hydration bug
messages: How should the dashboard fetch and cache server data?
Use TanStack Query for all server state in the dashboard: caching, deduping and background refetch come with it, and we keep no server data in component state.
Ok. Separate problem: the page logs a hydration mismatch error on first load.
The LastUpdated component calls Date.now() during render, so the server and the client render different text. Compute the timestamp in the route loader instead and pass it down.
Yes, the timestamp now comes from the loader and the hydration warning is gone in dev and in the production build.

distilled.summary: Chose the data layer and fixed a hydration mismatch.

decisions.text: Use TanStack Query for all server state in the dashboard

gotchas.text: Hydration mismatch came from Date.now() during render: compute timestamps in the route loader instead

sessions.title: Refetch behaviour
messages: Someone suggested moving to Redux for the dashboard. Thoughts?
Server data in the dashboard keeps going through TanStack Query, no Redux: the only client state we have is a few UI toggles.
Ok. The charts flicker whenever I switch tabs back to the dashboard.
That is refetchOnWindowFocus refetching every query. Turn it off by default and enable refetch on window focus only for the alerts panel queries, which must stay fresh.
Set refetchOnWindowFocus false in the QueryClient defaults and true on the alerts queries. No more flicker on the charts.

distilled.summary: Kept the data layer and limited focus refetching.

decisions.text: Refetch on window focus only for the alerts panel queries

sessions.title: Currency formatting
messages: Revenue figures show as 1234.5 instead of a proper amount.
Format currency with Intl.NumberFormat in the user's locale, style currency, so it reads $1,234.50 or 1.234,50 EUR depending on the browser.
Put it in a shared helper.
Added formatMoney(amount, currency) in lib/format.ts using Intl.NumberFormat and replaced the six ad hoc toFixed calls.
Added tests for en-US and de-DE output; both pass.

distilled.summary: Added locale-aware currency formatting.

decisions.text: Format currency with Intl.NumberFormat in the user's locale

sessions.title: Sync conflict strategy
messages: Two devices can edit the same note offline. How do we resolve conflicts when they sync?
Simplest is last-write-wins: every row has updated_at, and on sync the row with the newer updated_at replaces the other.
Implemented: resolve sync conflicts with last-write-wins on updated_at, in the merge step of the sync engine.
Added a test where two devices edit the same row; the later updated_at wins.

distilled.summary: Picked a first sync conflict strategy.

decisions.text: Resolve sync conflicts with last-write-wins on updated_at

sessions.title: Background sync locking errors
messages: Background sync fails with SQLITE_BUSY: database is locked, mostly while the user is typing.
The UI and the sync task each open their own writer connection and collide. Set busy_timeout to 5000 ms and route every write through a single writer connection.
And how often does sync run?
Sync runs every 15 minutes in the background and whenever the app comes to the foreground.
Done; a 30-minute soak test with typing and sync showed no SQLITE_BUSY errors.

distilled.summary: Fixed database locking during background sync.

decisions.text: Sync runs every 15 minutes in the background and on app foreground

gotchas.text: SQLITE_BUSY during background sync: set busy_timeout to 5000 ms and keep a single writer connection

sessions.title: Lost offline edits
messages: A tester lost edits: she changed the title on her phone offline and the body on her laptop, and after sync only one change survived.
That is last-write-wins dropping a whole row. We need a per-field merge: track a vector clock per field and merge field by field, so concurrent edits to different fields both survive.
What about two edits to the same field?
Then the clocks are concurrent and we keep both versions and flag the field for the user to pick.
The merge step now merges sync conflicts per field with vector clocks instead of last-write-wins; the tester's scenario keeps both edits.

distilled.summary: Replaced last-write-wins with per-field vector clock merges.

decisions.text: Merge sync conflicts per field with vector clocks instead of last-write-wins: LWW lost offline edits

sessions.title: Syncing deletions
messages: Deleted notes come back after a device that was offline for a week syncs.
The offline device still has the row and the server has no record it was deleted. Tombstone deleted rows for 30 days so offline devices can sync deletions.
Does this interact with the field merge?
A tombstone is just another field with its own clock, so the per-field vector clock merge stays as it is and handles it.
Added a deleted_at tombstone, a 30-day purge job, and a test with a week-offline device.

distilled.summary: Added tombstones so deletions sync.

decisions.text: Tombstone deleted rows for 30 days so offline devices can sync deletions

sessions.title: Speed up CI
messages: CI takes 25 minutes. Make it faster.
Two changes: cache the cargo registry and target dir with actions/cache keyed on Cargo.lock, and run the test suite on 4 parallel jobs.
With the cache warm the build step drops from 14 to 3 minutes, and 4 test jobs bring the whole run to 9 minutes.

distilled.summary: Cached cargo artifacts and parallelized tests in CI.

decisions.text: Cache the cargo registry and target dir in CI with actions/cache keyed on Cargo.lock
Run the test suite on 4 parallel jobs in CI

sessions.title: macOS runner out of memory
messages: The macOS job dies in the link step: the linker was killed, signal 9.
That is the linker running out of memory. Debug info for the test binaries is huge; set CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 in CI to cut it.
It still OOMs sometimes during tests.
Four parallel test jobs on the 7 GB macOS runner is too many. Run the test suite on 2 parallel jobs in CI: 4 jobs ran the macOS runner out of memory.
Set the parallelism to 2 and disabled dev debug info; ten consecutive runs passed, 11 minutes each.

distilled.summary: Fixed macOS CI memory exhaustion.

decisions.text: Run the test suite on 2 parallel jobs in CI: 4 jobs ran the macOS runner out of memory

gotchas.text: Linker OOM on the macOS runner: set CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 in CI

sessions.title: Release workflow
messages: Release tags follow vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, for example v1.4.0, and pushing such a tag triggers the publish workflow.
It builds the release binaries for the three platforms, uploads them to the GitHub release and publishes the crate.
Added a Releasing section to the README.

distilled.summary: Set up the tag-driven release workflow.

decisions.text: Release tags follow vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH and trigger the publish workflow

sessions.title: Token lifetimes
messages: Pick token lifetimes for the gateway.
Access tokens expire after 15 minutes, which limits the damage of a leaked token. Refresh tokens expire after 30 days.
Refresh tokens are stored hashed with SHA-256, never in plain text, so a database leak does not hand out sessions.
Implemented both in the token service with tests for expiry.

distilled.summary: Set token lifetimes and refresh token storage.

decisions.text: Access tokens expire after 15 minutes
Refresh tokens expire after 30 days and are stored hashed with SHA-256

sessions.title: Refresh loop
messages: Clients get stuck in a 401 loop when the access token expires.
The /auth/refresh route sits behind the auth middleware, so it demands the very access token that just expired and answers 401, and the client retries forever.
Exempt /auth/refresh from the auth middleware; it authenticates with the refresh token alone.
Yes, an expired access token now refreshes in one round trip; added an integration test.

distilled.summary: Fixed the token refresh 401 loop.

gotchas.text: 401 loop on token refresh: the /auth/refresh route sat behind the auth middleware; exempt it

sessions.title: Mobile refresh storms
messages: Mobile clients hammer the refresh endpoint; it is 40% of our traffic.
With 15-minute access tokens every open app refreshes four times an hour. Access tokens expire after 60 minutes instead: 15 minutes caused refresh storms on mobile.
Ok. Also someone is brute forcing logins.
Rate-limit /auth/login to 10 attempts per minute per IP, with a 429 and Retry-After.
Access token lifetime is now 60 minutes and the login limiter is live; refresh traffic dropped to 9%.

distilled.summary: Lengthened access tokens and rate-limited login.

decisions.text: Access tokens expire after 60 minutes: 15 minutes caused refresh storms on mobile
Rate-limit /auth/login to 10 attempts per minute per IP

sessions.title: Keyword search engine
messages: We need keyword search over the stored messages.
Use SQLite FTS5 with the porter tokenizer for message search: it is built into the bundled SQLite, and porter stemming matches 'indexing' to 'index'.
Porter is English-only, but our messages are almost all English. The FTS table adds about 30% to the database size.
Created the messages_fts virtual table with tokenize='porter unicode61' and triggers to keep it in sync.

distilled.summary: Built keyword search on FTS5.

decisions.text: Use SQLite FTS5 with the porter tokenizer for message search

sessions.title: Embedding pipeline
messages: Add semantic search. How do we split long messages for embedding?
Chunk messages at 512 tokens with 64 tokens of overlap before embedding, so a sentence at a boundary is in both chunks.
Startup now fails with: no such module: vec0.
The vec0 virtual table comes from the sqlite-vec extension, which must be loaded before opening the connection; we opened first and registered later.
Registered sqlite-vec with sqlite3_auto_extension before the first open; startup works and the vec_messages table is created.

distilled.summary: Built the embedding pipeline and fixed the vec0 load order.

decisions.text: Chunk messages at 512 tokens with 64 tokens of overlap before embedding

gotchas.text: 'no such module: vec0' at startup: load the sqlite-vec extension before opening the connection

sessions.title: Hybrid ranking
messages: Should semantic search replace the keyword engine?
No, message search stays on FTS5 with porter stemming; exact identifiers and error strings need keyword matching. We combine the two.
How do we combine the two result lists?
Fuse keyword and semantic hits with reciprocal rank fusion, k = 60. It needs no score normalization between BM25 and cosine.
Implemented fuse_rrf and a test where a hit ranked well in both lists comes first.

distilled.summary: Kept FTS5 and fused it with semantic results.

decisions.text: Fuse keyword and semantic hits with reciprocal rank fusion, k = 60

sessions.title: Money representation
messages: How should the billing API represent amounts?
Store money as integer cents in i64, never as floats: 0.1 + 0.2 is not 0.3 in floating point and invoices must add up exactly.
The API also sends integer cents plus an ISO 4217 currency code; clients format it.
Converted the Amount type to i64 cents and added a migration for the existing rows.

distilled.summary: Settled how money is represented.

decisions.text: Store money as integer cents in i64, never as floats

sessions.title: Invoice emails
messages: Customers should get an invoice email after checkout.
Simplest: send invoice emails synchronously inside the checkout request handler, right after the payment succeeds.
Added send_invoice_email to the checkout handler using the SMTP client.
The checkout test now asserts one email is sent per successful payment.

distilled.summary: Added invoice emails to checkout.

decisions.text: Send invoice emails synchronously inside the checkout request handler

sessions.title: Checkout stalls and duplicate charges
messages: Checkout sometimes hangs for 30 seconds, and two customers were charged twice yesterday.
The hang is the SMTP server stalling inside the request. Send invoice emails from a background job queue, not the request handler: SMTP stalls blocked checkout.
Stripe retried the payment webhook after our slow response and we processed it twice. Dedupe webhooks on an idempotency key taken from stripe_event_id.
Invoice emails now go through the job queue, and a unique index on stripe_event_id makes a retried webhook a no-op.

distilled.summary: Moved invoice emails to a queue and deduped webhooks.

decisions.text: Send invoice emails from a background job queue, not the request handler: SMTP stalls blocked checkout

gotchas.text: Duplicate charges from retried Stripe webhooks: dedupe on an idempotency key from stripe_event_id
